report:
Reviewed all three implementation entries and all three complete associated tests for immutable_entries. Requirements are append-only allocation, no safe mutable access to interned scalar/slice entries, and finalization of transient inference by resolution/copy into fresh storage. Captured storage-guide and architectural rationale specify that mutable inference relationships live outside the stash.

sage-stash::alloc and alloc_slice compute typed/content/count keys, return the existing entry for equal content, or append via push_raw. push_raw pads and extends the byte buffer and appends entry metadata; it does not overwrite earlier entries. Buffer growth copies the existing byte prefix, and resize_zeroed explicitly requires nondecreasing length. append_one constructs a new value vector and interns it rather than modifying the original slice. The public indexing implementations return shared references only; no IndexMut or mutable entry accessor is exposed. Stashed also exposes shared storage views, so retained results cannot be edited through those APIs.

The associated egraph::find follows version-local parent maps under shared access. Mutating inference operations update separate egraph maps; they do not replace Ty::InferVar allocations in the source stash. finalize_typed_body takes shared source/egraph references, constructs a new target stash, resolves each source type via find and expression slots via the completion table, and recursively allocates rebuilt body nodes. Its source memoization tables and target allocations are separate; unresolved infer variables panic instead of mutating source nodes into a result. The inspected copy paths include type/alias/call arguments, expression/statement/pattern slices and fields. This is an ownership/immutability assessment, not a review of authored expression semantics.

appending_and_deduplicating_preserves_existing_entries checks an existing scalar and slice after 4096 additions, then verifies reinterning equal values returns the original handles. safe_api_rejects_mutating_interned_scalars_and_slices visibly pins both attempted assignments in its body, runs trybuild compile_fail on both fixtures, and captured .stderr files require E0594 because IndexMut is absent. Thus compiler rejection is the intended API evidence, not an accidental runtime failure. finalized_nested_body_owns_resolved_and_imported_types_after_sources_drop checks source inference node, type/child slices, pending expression slot and imported bool remain unchanged after finalization; after dropping all source/proof storage it walks the destination tuple and literal children and asserts resolved bool types, stable spans and shared completed children. Together the tests exercise append/dedup stability, inaccessible safe mutation, and fresh finalization without in-place rewriting. They do not constitute an exhaustive proof for arbitrary unsafe client implementations; the claim is the safe allocated-entry API contract.

No TODO/N/A entries are associated. No source edits or tests executed in this review; commands were fresh review start/read and source inspection before record. The captured UI fixtures and expected diagnostics were inspected, not rerun. No requested edits.
